Deep Dive

Free full texts of the early Church Fathers and great saints. Links open on other sites.

Linked to the Apostles

Writers traditionally linked to the apostles or their disciples.

1 Clement

Clement of Rome

Letter to the church at Corinth, c. 96. Clement is traditionally said to have known Peter and Paul. New Advent: tr. John Keith (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 9).

Read at New Advent ↗ Also at Early Christian Writings ↗

Seven Letters

Ignatius of Antioch

Letters, c. 107–110, traditionally said to have been written on his way to martyrdom in Rome. New Advent: tr. Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1).

Read at New Advent:

Ephesians ↗ Magnesians ↗ Trallians ↗ Romans ↗ Philadelphians ↗ Smyrnaeans ↗ To Polycarp ↗

Letter to the Philippians

Polycarp of Smyrna

Letter, c. 110–140. According to Irenaeus, Polycarp was a disciple of St. John. New Advent: tr. Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1).

Read at New Advent ↗ Also at Early Christian Writings ↗

The Martyrdom of Polycarp

The Church of Smyrna

Letter of the church of Smyrna describing his death, c. 155. New Advent: tr. Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1).

Fragments

Papias of Hierapolis

Fragments, c. 115–140, of a collection of oral traditions about the apostles. New Advent: tr. Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1).

Fragment of his Apology

Quadratus of Athens

Fragment of an apology, c. 124–125, surviving in Eusebius, Church History IV.3 (chapter 3 on the New Advent page). New Advent: tr. Arthur Cushman McGiffert (Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, second series, vol. 1).
